rows.title: Turns and downturns in aging drivers.
rows.reason: The paper describes a system of in-vehicle sensors used to passively record driving behavior in older adults, which is one of the reader's kinds of systems.
rows.summary: Researchers studied 106 older adults' driving behavior over 12 weeks using in-vehicle sensors and found that those with greater cognitive decline were less likely to make left turns.

rows.title: Intrinsic capacity and mortality in community-dwelling octogenarians: a network analysis from the ilSIRENTE study.
rows.reason: The study uses routine home-based assessments to measure aspects of daily function in older adults, but the technology used is not one of the reader's kinds of systems.
rows.summary: This study used network analysis to examine the relationships between different aspects of intrinsic capacity (such as mobility, cognition, and sensory function) in older adults and found that mobility was a key factor in determining survival. The study also found that higher intrinsic capacity scores were associated with lower mortality. The study used routine home-based assessments to measure intrinsic capacity in a group of 319 community-dwelling adults aged 80 and older.

rows.title: Validation of socialbit as a smartwatch algorithm for social interaction detection in a clinical population.
rows.reason: The paper describes a system of one of the profile's kinds (a smartwatch-based system) used to measure social interaction in older adults, but the focus is on the algorithm's validation rather than its building or deployment.
rows.summary: Researchers developed a smartwatch algorithm called SocialBit to detect social interactions in people with and without neurological deficits, and tested it in 153 hospitalized stroke patients with varying levels of stroke severity and cognition. The algorithm achieved high accuracy and maintained performance in patients with language deficits. The study found that patients with more severe strokes engaged in less social interaction.

rows.title: Requirements of health professionals and affected persons for an App-based dual-task training for hearing impaired older adults - a Delphi survey.
rows.reason: The paper discusses the development of a system for hearing-impaired older adults, but it is not about building, validating, deploying, or using a system of one of the profile's kinds, with older adults, to measure cognition or daily function.
rows.summary: A Delphi survey of health professionals and hearing-impaired older adults identified key themes for a tailored cognitive-motor training app, including app features, exercise characteristics, and feedback. The results showed consensus on some aspects, but also significant differences between the two groups. The study suggests that digital dual-task training programs should be flexible and user-centered to promote engagement and improved outcomes.

rows.title: AI-Powered Framework for Personalized Prescription of Physical Activity in Aging: Proposing PEPHA, a framework for Personalized Phenotyping for Aging.
rows.reason: The paper describes a system that is one of the profile's kinds of systems (a system that uses wearable data to measure physical activity and sedentary behavior in older adults), but its main focus is on the AI framework and its application, rather than the system itself.
rows.summary: This paper proposes a framework called PEPHA that uses AI to analyze wearable data and identify personalized, time-specific patterns of physical activity and sedentary behavior associated with cognitive functioning and mental health in older adults. The framework was tested on a cohort of 67 older adults and found that individualized analyses could uncover distinct behavioral patterns correlated with cognitive functioning and mental health. The results suggest that PEPHA could be used to inform personalized physical activity interventions in aging.

rows.title: Detection of depression risk among older adults using home-deployed socially assistive robots: a real-world study.
rows.reason: The paper describes a system of one of the reader's kinds (a socially assistive robot) with older adults, but its main focus is on the robot's ability to detect depression, not on building or validating the system.
rows.summary: A study used a socially assistive robot to monitor older adults' behavior and detect depression risk, with a model that predicted symptomatic participants with a sensitivity of 0.939.

rows.title: From wrist data to lifespan: elucidating inflammation-driven biological aging via activity rhythms captured by wearable devices.
rows.reason: The paper describes using wearable devices to measure activity rhythms and physical activity in older adults, which is one of the reader's kinds of systems, to study its relationship with inflammation and mortality.
rows.summary: Researchers used wearable devices to study how daily activity rhythms and physical activity are linked to inflammation and mortality in older adults, finding that improving these rhythms can mitigate the effects of inflammation on survival.

rows.title: Eye movements powered by artificial intelligence identify asymptomatic carriers of familial Alzheimer's disease.
rows.reason: The paper uses eye-tracking technology, which is one of the profile's kinds of systems, but it's focused on a specific population (Alzheimer's disease carriers) and outcome (detection of asymptomatic carriers), rather than building or validating the system itself.
rows.summary: Researchers used eye-tracking technology and machine learning to identify people who are carriers of a genetic mutation that increases their risk of developing Alzheimer's disease, even if they don't show any symptoms.

rows.title: Remote Online-Based Application of the Cerebellar Cognitive Affective Syndrome Scale.
rows.reason: The paper discusses the remote administration of a cognitive assessment tool, which is one of the profile's kinds of systems, but its main focus is on the tool's suitability and reliability rather than its development or deployment.
rows.summary: A study evaluated the suitability of a cognitive assessment tool, the Cerebellar Cognitive Affective Syndrome Scale, for remote administration via video. The results showed that remote administration was feasible and reliable, but more research is needed to establish measurement equivalence between remote and in-person administration. The study compared remote and in-person administration in patients with cerebellar disease and controls.

rows.title: Feasibility and Acceptability of a Remote Sleep-Dependent Memory Assessment in Older Adults With Cognitive Concerns: Pilot Cross-Sectional Study.
rows.reason: The Sleep Memories app is a type of system mentioned in the reader's profile, but its main focus is on assessing sleep-dependent memory consolidation, not daily function or cognition in general.
rows.summary: A mobile app, Sleep Memories, was tested with older adults to assess their sleep-dependent memory consolidation. The app was found to be feasible and acceptable, with 68 participants completing at least one test. User feedback was positive, but some participants experienced minor technical issues.

rows.title: Remote cognitive training for older adults using tablets: A pilot trial.
rows.reason: The paper describes a system of one of the reader's kinds (a self-administered web-based or tablet-based cognitive assessment) being used to measure cognition in older adults.
rows.summary: A pilot trial tested a tablet-based cognitive training program for older adults with cognitive impairment or dementia, finding improved cognitive function in those who used the tablet compared to those who used a TV interface.

rows.title: Videoconference-integrated, computer-assisted cognitive testing improves the remote assessment of processing speed and attention.
rows.reason: The paper discusses the use of a videoconference-integrated system, which is one of the profile's kinds of systems, to measure cognition in older adults, but the main focus is on comparing different versions of cognitive tests rather than the system itself.
rows.summary: Researchers compared in-person and remote videoconference-based assessments of cognitive processing speed and attention using various versions of two standard tests. They found that a digital version of one test was as effective as the in-person version, while an oral version was less effective. The study suggests that remote videoconference-based assessments with digital tasks could be a useful tool for cognitive testing.

rows.title: Effect of Multi-Modal Training in Patients With Mild Cognitive Impairment: A Randomized Controlled Pilot Trial.
rows.reason: The paper describes a system combining exercise, computerized cognitive training, and reminiscence therapy, which is adjacent to the reader's kinds of systems, but with a different population and outcome.
rows.summary: A 24-week multi-modal training program combining exercise, computerized cognitive training, and reminiscence therapy improved cognitive function in older adults with mild cognitive impairment compared to health education alone.

rows.title: Cognitive behavioural therapy for older adults with depressive symptoms living in residential aged care: A pilot study of a systemic treatment model.
rows.reason: The paper discusses a therapy program for older adults with depression, but it does not involve technology, which is a key aspect of the reader's profile.
rows.summary: A pilot study tested a 5-month therapy program for older adults with depression in residential care, led by supervised students, with some family and staff involvement. The program showed high participant satisfaction and some promising clinical outcomes. The study suggests that a larger trial is warranted to confirm the program's effectiveness.

rows.title: An exploratory descriptive qualitative study examining the experiences and perceptions of family caregivers engaging in structured home-based reminiscence activities with persons with dementia.
rows.reason: The paper discusses a reminiscence activity, which is one of the profile's kinds of systems, but it is not the focus of the paper, and the population and outcome are the same as the profile's, but the technology is a package, not a system built or operated by the reader.
rows.summary: This study explored the experiences of family caregivers in Singapore who used a structured reminiscence package to engage with people with dementia at home. The caregivers found the package easy to use and reported benefits such as fostering relational connection and engagement. However, they also noted the need for personalization and cultural resonance of the materials.

rows.title: Cortisol awakening response and autobiographical memory in healthy older adults: The moderating role of negative reminiscence.
rows.reason: The paper discusses a population and outcome of interest, but uses a different kind of technology (saliva samples) and focuses on a different aspect of cognition (autobiographical memory) rather than building or using a system to measure cognition or daily function.
rows.summary: This study examined the relationship between cortisol awakening response, negative reminiscence, and autobiographical memory in healthy older adults, finding that the cortisol response predicted less specific memories, but only in those with high negative reminiscence.

rows.title: From digital companionship to capability building: reframing conversational artificial intelligence and older adults' psychological wellbeing in active aging.
rows.reason: The paper discusses the use of conversational AI with older adults, but its main focus is on the conceptual framework and its implications, rather than the technology itself.
rows.summary: This paper argues that conversational AI should be seen as a tool to build older adults' capabilities, rather than just providing companionship, and proposes a framework to understand how this works.

rows.title: Addressing the silent epidemic: a narrative review and evidence synthesis of digital health and telehealth interventions for loneliness in older adults.
rows.reason: The paper discusses technology-based interventions for loneliness in older adults, but it is not focused on building, validating, or using systems to measure cognition or daily function.
rows.summary: The paper reviews digital health and telehealth interventions for loneliness in older adults, finding that some interventions, such as telehealth video visits and digital mental health platforms, show promise in reducing loneliness and depression.

rows.title: Social needs in home care for older adults: A qualitative exploration of recognition, expectations and opportunities.
rows.reason: The paper discusses the importance of social interaction in home care, but does not focus on building, validating, or using technology to measure cognition or daily function in older adults.
rows.summary: The study explores how older adults, their families, and caregivers perceive and address social needs in home care, highlighting the importance of small acts of kindness and social interaction in care provision.

rows.title: Evaluating the Effectiveness of Digital Social Robots in Reducing Loneliness Among Community-Dwelling Older Adults in Japan: Randomized Controlled Trial and Qualitative Analysis.
rows.reason: The paper is about using a social robot, which is a different kind of technology from the ones mentioned in the reader's profile, but it does focus on older adults and loneliness, which are relevant to the reader's interests.
rows.summary: A study in Japan found that a digital social robot reduced loneliness and improved well-being in older adults living alone, and identified categories of benefits including emotional support and lifestyle assistance.

rows.title: Bridging language markers and pathology: correlations between digital speech measures and surrogate CSF biomarkers in Alzheimer's disease.
rows.reason: The paper discusses the use of a conversational engagement system with older adults, but its main focus is on the correlations between language markers and CSF biomarkers, rather than the system itself.
rows.summary: A study found correlations between digital speech measures and cerebrospinal fluid biomarkers in Alzheimer's disease, suggesting that conversational language could be used for early detection and monitoring.

rows.title: Bridging Language Markers and Pathology: Correlations Between Digital Speech Measures and Surrogate CSF Biomarkers in Alzheimer's Disease.
rows.reason: The paper uses a conversational system with older adults, but its focus is on linking language markers to biomarkers, not on building or using the system itself.
rows.summary: Researchers used machine learning to link digital language markers from a conversational study to cerebrospinal fluid biomarkers of Alzheimer's disease, finding correlations between language complexity and biomarkers.

rows.title: Systemic sclerosis in 2026: emerging paradigms from the World Scleroderma Congress.
rows.reason: The paper is about a different disease and technology, with no mention of older adults, cognition, or daily function.
rows.summary: The paper discusses recent advances in understanding and treating systemic sclerosis, a chronic autoimmune disease, including new diagnostic methods and therapeutic strategies.

rows.title: Recent advances in tumor microenvironment-responsive pro-antibody to overcome on-target, off-tumor toxicity.
rows.reason: The paper is about a new type of antibody therapy, not a system for measuring cognition or daily function in older adults.
rows.summary: This review discusses a new type of antibody therapy that can target tumors more specifically by responding to the unique biochemical conditions of the tumor microenvironment, reducing the risk of side effects.

rows.title: uPAR-Targeting T Cell Engager Exerts Senolytic Effects in Mice and Non-Human Primates With Serum Aminotransferase Activity as a Safety Monitor.
rows.reason: The paper discusses a senolytic therapy, but it is not a system of one of the reader's kinds, such as a sensor network or a web-based cognitive assessment.
rows.summary: Researchers developed a new type of senolytic therapy that targets senescent cells using a bispecific T-cell engager, which was effective in eliminating senescent cells and alleviating age-related pathologies in mice and non-human primates without adverse effects.

rows.title: Oncofetal antigens as emerging targets in chimeric antigen receptor (CAR)-T cell-based immunotherapies: opportunities and challenges.
rows.reason: The paper is about CAR-T cell therapies, but it does not mention older adults or any of the reader's kinds of systems.
rows.summary: Researchers discuss the potential of oncofetal antigens as targets for CAR-T cell therapies, highlighting both promising results and challenges in treating solid malignancies.

rows.title: Oral Health Care Interventions by Functional Status Among Older Adults in a Nursing Home and Day Care Centre: A Pilot Study.
rows.reason: The paper is about a system (oral health care program) of one of the profile's kinds, but with a different population and outcome (oral health instead of cognition or daily function).
rows.summary: A pilot study found that a tailored oral health care program improved oral hygiene in older adults in nursing homes and day care centers, regardless of their functional status.

rows.title: Disparities in Dental Care Access, Oral Cancer Counseling, and Oral Cancer Examination Among U.S. Adults with a History of Cancer: Results from NHANES, 2015-2018.
rows.reason: The paper is about oral health services, but does not involve any of the reader's areas of expertise in technology for aging research.
rows.summary: This study found that US adults with a history of cancer were more likely to receive oral cancer counseling and exams, but still had disparities in access to dental care.

rows.title: Periodontitis, Edentulism, and Accelerated Biological Aging: A Population-Based Study of Epigenetic Clocks.
rows.reason: The paper is about the relationship between oral health and aging, but it does not involve the kinds of systems described in the reader's profile.
rows.summary: This study found that severe periodontitis and edentulism are linked to accelerated aging in older adults, as measured by epigenetic clocks.

rows.title: Frailty in Cardiorenal Care: A Geriatric Perspective on the 2026 European Society of Cardiology Guidelines.
rows.reason: The paper discusses older adults and their health outcomes, but it is not about building, validating, deploying, or using a system of one of the reader's kinds, such as in-home sensor networks or web-based cognitive assessments.
rows.summary: This editorial proposes a new framework for cardiorenal care in older adults, incorporating frailty and other factors to improve treatment decisions and patient outcomes.
